name: Ringo Street Vendor Cart
description: A motorized vendor cart manufactured by Ringo, the corponation that quietly dominates Tier 1-2 street commerce. Electric drive, fold-out serving counter, integrated heating/cooling, and a surprisingly sophisticated inventory tracking system. Ringo doesn't sell these carts — they lease them, and the lease agreement gives Ringo access to every transaction, every location, and every customer interaction. The carts are affordable. The data extraction is the real product.
common_usage: Street food vendors, mobile repair shops, pop-up retail, roaming medical aid stations.
story_hooks: A vendor discovers their Ringo cart has been recording customer conversations and uploading them nightly
Ringo uses vendor cart location data to map human movement patterns with higher accuracy than any surveillance system
physical_description: A boxy, reinforced polymer cart roughly the size of a food truck, painted in Ringo's signature corporate gray with faded neon accent strips along the edges. The serving counter folds out from the front with worn stainless steel surfaces, while a compact electric motor hums beneath a weathered chassis scarred by years of street-level use. Rain-slicked surfaces reflect the glow of its integrated LED menu display, and a small antenna protrudes from the roof—constantly syncing transaction data back to Ringo's servers.
visual_prompt: gritty motorized vendor cart, corporate gray polymer chassis, worn stainless steel serving counter, faded neon accent strips, rain-slicked surfaces, compact electric motor, data antenna, neo-noir street commerce, cyberpunk aesthetics, detailed product photography, dark rainy background, industrial decay, worn metal and plastic materials, moody neon reflection
